Aether Biotech - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Aether Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Aether Biotech's financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Priya Singh, Chief Medical Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of Aether Biotech.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Jordan. Good morning, everyone. Aether Biotech delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust volume growth in our oncology and cardio-renal franchises, alongside effective lifecycle management and sales execution. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including navigating patent cliff exposure through innovative life cycle management strategies, enhancing marketing and sales effectiveness, optimizing our position in the pricing and reimbursement landscape, and delivering on overall performance highlights that position us for sustained growth.

We're particularly excited about the subcutaneous auto-injector version of AETH-401 and its potential to drive label expansions, capture additional market share in metastatic NSCLC, and extend our competitive moat well into the next decade.

Now, I will turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $2,850 million, an increase of 22% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by strong volume expansion in oncology and immunology, fueled by AETH-301 and AETH-412, partially offset by pricing headwinds and biosimilar erosion in legacy assets.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $380 million, or $1.45 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $505 million, or $1.92 per share.

Our operating expenses were $1,370 million, reflecting disciplined investment in high-ROI R&D programs at $950 million and SG&A at $420 million. We continue to invest heavily in R&D to support our pipeline, including topline data from the Phase 3 AETHERON trial. Our cash position remains strong at $4.2 billion.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us on Aether Biotech's third-quarter 2024 earnings call. I'm pleased to walk you through our overall performance highlights, which underscore another quarter of robust execution amid a dynamic biotech landscape. Q3 total revenues came in at $2.85 billion, representing 22% year-over-year growth and a 5% beat against our guidance midpoint. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, driven primarily by volume expansion in our core oncology and immunology franchises, partially offset by the anticipated pricing headwinds in the U.S. GLP-1 market. On a constant-currency basis, growth was even stronger at 24%, reflecting solid international momentum.

Non-GAAP EPS was $1.92, up 28% year-over-year and exceeding our $1.75 to $1.85 guide by $0.07. GAAP EPS came in at $1.45, reflecting a one-time $120 million charge related to the in-licensing of a next-gen ADC payload. Adjusted for that, our underlying profitability remains on track, with gross margins expanding 210 basis points to 82.5%—a testament to our manufacturing efficiencies at our Singapore biologics facility and favorable mix shift toward higher-margin specialty products.

Let me break this down by key drivers. Oncology, which accounts for 55% of revenues, delivered $1.57 billion, up 31% YoY, fueled by AETH-301, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody, which generated $920 million in global sales—surpassing Keytruda's early U.S. launch trajectory on a per-patient basis. We saw 42% volume growth here, bolstered by label expansions into frontline NSCLC and HCC, with U.S. TRx share now at 28% per IQVIA data, closing the gap on leaders like Merck and Roche. Immunology contributed $850 million, up 15% YoY, led by AETH-412, our IL-23 inhibitor, which captured 19% of the U.S. moderate-to-severe psoriasis market, nipping at the heels of Tremfya and Skyrizi amid biosimilar erosion for Stelara.

Regionally, the U.S. remained our growth engine at 62% of revenues—$1.77 billion, up 26% YoY—despite the IRA's price negotiation pilots impacting our legacy hypertension portfolio by ~$45 million. Europe delivered $580 million, a 17% increase on a reported basis and 21% constant-currency, thanks to reimbursement wins for AETH-301 in Germany and France, where we've now achieved HTA approval across all five major markets. Emerging markets, at 12% of the mix, grew 35% to $340 million, with China partnerships—like our co-commercialization deal with Innovent for AETH-412—driving outsized gains; APAC TRx for that asset jumped 52% QoQ.

On the expense side, R&D spend was $950 million, or 33% of revenues, up 12% YoY but flat sequentially as we prioritized high-ROI programs. Key technical initiatives included positive topline from the Phase 3 AETHERON trial of AETH-512, our CRISPR-based CAR-T for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, showing a 68% ORR and 52% CR rate versus 45% for standard-of-care Abecma—data we'll file with FDA by year-end, targeting a Q2 2025 PDUFA. We also advanced our ADCs with a $250 million upfront for the payload, enhancing our pipeline's best-in-class potential.

SG&A came in at $420 million, disciplined at 15% of sales, reflecting our digital commercialization push via AI-driven HCP targeting, which improved our CAC by 18%. Operating cash flow was a stellar $1.1 billion, enabling $500 million in share repurchases and dividends, with net debt now at 1.2x EBITDA—well within our target leverage.

Challenges were manageable: U.S. pricing pressure shaved 300 bps off growth, biosimilar launches for our off-patent interferon portfolio cost us $80 million, and FX headwinds in JPY and EUR deducted 200 bps. Yet, we navigated these with proactive hedging and pipeline derisking.

Strategically, we're leaning into three pillars: oncology dominance via next-gen modalities like bispecifics and ADCs, with five Phase 3 readouts expected H2 2025; GLP-1 adjacencies, where our oral small-molecule GIP/GLP-1 agonist entered Phase 2b, positioning us against Zepbound and Mounjaro in a $100B+ TAM; and M&A firepower, with $4.2 billion in dry powder post our tuck-in acquisition of a radiopharma platform, targeting alpha-emitters for PSMA-positive prostate cancer.

Key takeaways: Q3 validates our '24 guidance—full-year revenues now $11.2-11.5 billion, up from prior guide, non-GAAP EPS $7.40-7.60, raised $0.10—and sets up '25 for 18-20% growth. Our 12 commercialized products, 18 Phase 3 assets, and $15B+ peak sales visibility give us conviction in delivering 15%+ CAGR through the decade, outpacing peers like Regeneron and Vertex.

Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. This is Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO of Aether Biotech, taking a few minutes to dive deeper into our patent cliff exposure and the robust life cycle management strategies we've deployed to mitigate it. As you know, the pharma industry faces a $300 billion global patent cliff through 2030, per Evaluate Pharma estimates, with heavy hitters like AbbVie's Humira—already down 35% YoY post-biosimilar entry—and Eli Lilly's blockbuster GLP-1s like Mounjaro staring down U.S. composition-of-matter patent challenges as early as 2031. For Aether, we're proactively ahead of this curve, with a diversified portfolio and innovative lifecycle tactics that have preserved over 65% of at-risk revenues to date.

Let's start with our exposure. Our top three revenue drivers—AETH-401, our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific oncology antibody generating $2.8 billion in 2023 sales, 42% of total revenue; AETH-278, the SGLT2/GLP-1 combo for cardio-renal-diabetic indications at $1.9 billion, 29%; and AETH-156, our inhaled long-acting muscarinic antagonist for COPD at $1.2 billion, 18%—represent 89% of our $6.7 billion top-line. AETH-401's core composition-of-matter patent expires in Q4 2027 in the U.S., followed by Europe in 2028 under supplementary protection certificate extensions. Without intervention, IQVIA models suggest an 85-90% first-year generic/biosimilar erosion, akin to Keytruda's projected $25 billion U.S. cliff in 2028 or Merck's $7 billion Januvia drop-off post-2026. For AETH-278, Orange Book-listed method-of-use patents hold until 2032, but Paragraph IV challenges from Teva and Mylan could accelerate that to 2029. AETH-156 faces EU expiry in 2026, with minimal U.S. protection beyond pediatric exclusivity ending mid-2027.

Cumulative projected cliff impact? Base case: $4.2 billion revenue headwind through 2030, or 25% of our pro forma 2028 run-rate, assuming 70% average erosion. But here's where our lifecycle management shines—we've clawed back $1.1 billion in preserved value YTD through layered IP strategies, outperforming peers like Bristol Myers Squibb, which saw 40% erosion on Opdivo post-cliff analogs.

Our lifecycle playbook is multifaceted, blending regulatory, formulation, and commercial levers. First, formulation evergreening: For AETH-401, we've launched a subcutaneous Q2W auto-injector version via 505(b)(2) pathway—FDA-approved last quarter—extending data exclusivity to 2033 and capturing 15% market share in metastatic NSCLC within three months, mirroring Amgen's Repatha switch success. This drove a 12% label expansion uplift, with U.S. pricing at parity but 20% volume growth from IV-weary patients. In Europe, EMA granted 8+3 years for this line extension, buffering biosimilar entry.

Second, indication expansions and combinations: AETH-278's Phase III readout in H1 2024 for NASH/MASH positions it for sNDA filing Q3, leveraging the same API with a fixed-dose combo add-on for hypertension—projected $800 million peak sales by 2029, extending overall franchise IP to 2035 via new formulation patents. We've seen 25% share gains in Type 2 diabetes combos, similar to Novo Nordisk's Ozempic-to-Rybelsus pivot, which mitigated 15% of early erosion.

Third, pediatric and orphan designations: AETH-156 snagged six months pediatric exclusivity in the U.S. for adolescent COPD, pushing cliff to 2028, while orphan status for rare interstitial lung disease adds seven years EU market exclusivity—already booking $150 million in off-label EU tenders.

Regionally, we're tailored: In the U.S., aggressive Hatch-Waxman litigation has settled 70% of ANDA Paragraph IVs favorably, with $500 million in authorized generics retaining 10-15% share post-cliff, like Pfizer's Viagra model. Europe benefits from pediatric investigation plans and SPCs, holding AETH-401 to 2030 despite EMA biosimilar approvals looming. Japan PMDA granted re-examination periods for AETH-278, adding 10 years via partial changes. In emerging markets—China and India, 12% of our sales—we've out-licensed to local partners like Sinopharm, securing royalties through 2032 while navigating compulsory licensing risks via WHO-prequalified status.

Strategically, we're diversifying beyond the cliff: Our $2.5 billion M&A war chest funded the $1.2 billion acquisition of Helix Oncology last year, bolstering the AETH-401 franchise with next-gen ADCs entering Phase II, targeting $3 billion peak by 2032. Internally, 40% of R&D spend ($1.8 billion in 2023) fuels 12 late-stage assets, with four label extensions in clinic. Biosimilar defenses include patent thickets—average 18 Orange Book listings per molecule—and value-based pricing contracts covering 60% of U.S. lives, limiting rebates to 25% post-erosion.

Looking forward, lifecycle strategies offsetting 60% of 2025-2027 cliff impacts. Adjusted EBITDA margins hold at 38-40%, supported by 15% OpEx discipline. Risks? Accelerated litigation losses or FTC scrutiny on patent settlements, but our 85% win rate pegs downside at <$500 million. We're not just surviving the cliff—we're leaping over it, positioning Aether as a top-15 global player by 2030 with $15 billion revenue potential.

Good afternoon, everyone. Before I hand over for more strategic updates, I'd like to dive deep into our marketing and sales effectiveness metrics, which continue to underpin our robust top-line growth of 22% year-over-year for our flagship portfolio. Aether Biotech is laser-focused on our immuno-oncology franchise, led by AETH-401—our PD-1/PD-L1 bispecific antibody that's capturing share in the metastatic NSCLC and melanoma markets—and our recently launched gene therapy, GeneVita, for rare genetic disorders like SMA. Our team has executed flawlessly against a challenging backdrop of biosimilar erosion from Keytruda biosimilars entering Europe and ongoing Inflation Reduction Act pricing pressures in the U.S.

Let me start with the headline metrics. Total prescriptions—or TRx—for AETH-401 grew 22% YoY to 1.2 million scripts in Q3, outpacing the branded IO market's 12% expansion per IQVIA data. New Rx—or NRx—momentum was even stronger at 28% YoY, reflecting our success in line extensions and combo regimens with checkpoint partners like Bristol Myers' Opdivo. Market share for AETH-401 in first-line NSCLC climbed to 14.2% from 11.8% a year ago, while in melanoma, we're now at 16.5%, gaining 210 basis points sequentially. For GeneVita, early launch metrics are stellar: 45,000 NRx in its first full quarter post-approval, with 92% payer coverage at launch across commercial formularies.

Sales force effectiveness remains a core strength. Our 1,200-strong U.S. field team averaged 8.2 high-quality HCP details per rep per week, up 15% from Q3 2023, driven by our AI-powered territory optimization tool, AetherTarget AI. This platform, built in partnership with Veeva Systems, uses machine learning to prioritize high-decile prescribers based on historical TRx lift, electronic health record data, and real-time competitor activity. The result? A 24% improvement in reach-and-frequency scores, with top-tier oncologists receiving 4.2 details per month versus the industry benchmark of 3.1. Detailing ROI hit $4.20 in incremental AETH-401 revenue per detail dollar spent—well above our internal hurdle of $3.50 and Merck's reported $3.80 for Keytruda.

Shifting to digital and omnichannel channels, which now account for 35% of our total HCP engagements—up from 22% two years ago. Our myAetherHCP portal saw 2.3 million unique logins in Q3, a 41% YoY surge, with email click-through rates on personalized CME content at 28%, double the pharma average. We're leveraging closed-loop marketing with Salesforce integration to track omnichannel attribution: 62% of digital touchpoints convert to a lift in NRx within 30 days, per our proprietary analytics. Patient services are another accelerator—our AetherSupport hub enrolled 78,000 patients on AETH-401, reducing discontinuation rates by 11% through copay assistance and adherence apps, which indirectly boosts HCP loyalty.

Regionally, performance is bifurcated but trending positively. In the U.S., which drove 72% of portfolio sales, TRx growth was 25% YoY, fueled by 95% Medicare Part D coverage and our DTC campaign via TV and social, reaching 15 million impressions with a 2.1% lift in brand awareness per Nielsen. Share of voice—or SoV—stood at 18% in IO digital media, ahead of Regeneron's Libtayo. Europe faced headwinds from HTA delays and German AMNOG pricing, limiting growth to 9% YoY, but we're countering with localized KOL programs—engaging 450 key opinion leaders across Germany, France, and Italy—and expect sequential acceleration to 15% in H2 as we secure NICE recommendation in the UK. Emerging markets are our growth engine: Asia-Pacific sales jumped 42% YoY, led by China approvals for AETH-401 via our partnership with Sinopharm, where NRx share hit 8% in urban tier-1 cities. Latin America added 30% growth via Brazil's ANVISA nod for GeneVita.

On trends, we're seeing a clear shift toward value-based metrics amid payer scrutiny. Customer acquisition cost—or CAC—for new HCP prescribers fell 17% to $1,450, thanks to predictive analytics reducing low-yield calls by 30%. Biosimilar competition remains a drag—TRx share loss to adalimumab follow-ons was 3% in our legacy RA portfolio—but our pipeline hedges this with three Phase 3 readouts in 2025. Marketing spend efficiency improved to a 4.8x ROI overall, with tactical reallocations: we cut low-ROI journal ads by 20% and doubled investment in AI-driven micro-targeting.

Strategically, we're doubling down on three initiatives. First, expanding AetherTarget AI to Europe and Asia by year-end, projecting a 20% sales productivity lift. Second, our 'Patient Journey 360' omnichannel platform, integrating HCP detailing with patient apps and payer data via real-world evidence from TriNetX, to drive adherence and extensions. Third, strategic alliances—like our co-promotion deal with AstraZeneca for combo IO regimens—to amplify reach without proportional headcount growth.

In summary, our marketing and sales engine is firing on all cylinders, delivering sustainable share gains and efficiency in a maturing IO market projected to hit $120 billion globally by 2028 per Evaluate Pharma. We guide full-year TRx growth at 20-22%, with sales force productivity up mid-teens.

Thank you, Operator, and good afternoon, everyone. This is Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO of Aether Biotech. I'll now turn to our pricing and reimbursement landscape, which remains a dynamic and critical area for our business, particularly as we navigate the post-IRA environment in the US, evolving HTA frameworks globally, and the rise of biosimilars across our portfolio.

In Q3, our portfolio realized a blended net price of $1.42 billion, up 4% year-over-year on a reported basis, but flat on an ex-foreign exchange and inflation-adjusted basis. This reflects disciplined pricing strategies amid headwinds from payer pushback and biosimilar competition. Gross-to-net deductions averaged 38% across our US commercial book—up 200 basis points from last year—driven primarily by higher rebates to PBMs like Express Scripts and CVS Caremark, which now account for 62% of our covered lives. Our WAC increases were modest at 5.2% for our flagship oncology asset, AETH-401, with peak sales potential north of $8 billion, aligning with the industry's 4-6% norm to minimize list price scrutiny under the Inflation Reduction Act.

Turning to the US, the IRA's maximum fair price negotiations continue to cast a long shadow. AETH-401 dodged the initial seven drugs selected for 2026 negotiation—unlike Eli Lilly's Mounjaro or Merck's Keytruda—but we're bracing for potential inclusion post-2028 given its $2.1 billion in Medicare Part D spend last year. We've proactively layered in value-based agreements, or VBAs, covering 28% of AETH-401 lives, with rebates tied to PFS milestones like ORR above 45% and mPFS exceeding 14 months in real-world evidence from our ongoing RWD registry with Flatiron Health. These VBAs have stabilized net pricing at 68% of WAC, versus the portfolio average of 62%. On the 340B front, discounts hit 48% of WAC, but our carve-out strategy with Optum has limited exposure to just 12% of TRx volume.

Commercial reimbursement remains robust at 92% for AETH-401, with formulary placement on Tier 2 for 85% of lives under UnitedHealthcare and Anthem. However, we're seeing early pressure from biosimilar entrants—Amgen's version of our legacy TNF inhibitor captured 18% share in Q3, eroding our volumes by 12% and compressing ASP by 22%. We've countered with a patient copay assistance program capping out-of-pocket at $10/month for 95% of eligible patients, boosting adherence to 87% at six months per IQVIA data.

Shifting to Europe, which represents 22% of our ex-US revenue, the landscape is fragmented but stabilizing post-COVID backlogs. In Germany, IQWiG's early benefit assessments granted AETH-401 a "major additional benefit" rating, securing AMNOG reimbursement at our proposed price—€78,000 per course—without clawbacks. France's HAS followed suit with an SMR of "important," though we accepted a 7% managed entry agreement discount phased over 24 months. The UK's NICE issued a positive final appraisal for AETH-401 in Q2, recommending it within the Cancer Drugs Fund at list, preserving £1.2 billion in five-year sales potential. Across the EU5, our blended reimbursement rate is 89%, but confidential discounts average 22%, reflecting the push for multi-indication HTA harmonization under the EU HTA Regulation effective 2025.

Italy and Spain continue to lag, with AIFA and AEMPS approvals pending real-world cost-effectiveness data; we're submitting ICER analyses showing €42,000 per QALY gained versus standard-of-care, benchmarked against Roche's Tecentriq. Biosimilar erosion is more acute here—our hemophilia A gene therapy lost 15% market share to Pfizer's biosimilar entrant, prompting a 10% ASP cut to maintain NRDL inclusion in select tenders.

In Japan, PMDA reimbursement for AETH-401 holds at JPY 12.5 million per cycle, with 95% coverage under the NHI premium pricing scheme—our advocacy through JPMA helped secure this despite the biennial drug price revisions capping hikes at 1.8%. China, our fastest-growing market at 31% YoY growth to RMB 850 million, saw our gene therapy added to the NRDL Volume-Based Procurement in Q3 at a 52% discount off list—but volumes surged 45%, delivering flat net revenue impact. We're piloting outcomes-based pilots with Ping An Good Doctor, refunding 20% if annualized bleed rates exceed 2.5 per patient.

Emerging markets like Brazil and India contribute 8% of revenue but face acute pricing pressures; ANVISA reimbursement for AETH-401 is at 65% of US WAC, supported by our tech transfer partnership with Hetero Drugs for local fill-finish, reducing logistics costs by 18%.

Strategically, we're ahead of the curve on several fronts. First, our RWE platform, integrated with TriNetX and Symphony Health claims database, has generated 15 label expansions supporting pricing parity—think AETH-401 in MSI-high solid tumors, mirroring Bristol Myers' Opdivo playbook. Second, we've inked co-pay accumulator carve-outs with 14 PBMs, shielding 40% of commercial lives from accumulator programs that have eroded adherence for peers like Regeneron’s Eylea. Third, our biosimilar defense includes lifecycle management: AETH-401-2, our next-gen bispecific with ADCC enhancement, files BLA in H1 2025, projecting 25% potency uplift and potential premium pricing.

Looking forward, we expect US gross-to-net to trend to 40% by year-end, with EU discounts stable at 20-25%. Biosimilars will pressure legacy assets, but our innovative pipeline—six Phase 3 readouts in 2025—positions us for 7-9% pricing growth. We're also ramping advocacy via PhRMA and EFPIA for IRA reforms and HTA transparency.

In summary, while the landscape is challenging, our proactive pricing architecture, VBA adoption, and RWE investments have delivered resilient net realization—our strongest in three years.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenues of $11.2-11.5 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $7.40-7.60.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you, Elena. We will now open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Citi. Please go ahead.

John Smith, Citi:
Thanks, and good morning. Great results overall. Elena, could you expand a bit more on the patent cliff mitigation for AETH-401 specifically? With the subcu launch, how much of that 85-90% erosion risk do you think you've offset, and any updates on the Paragraph IV settlements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Thanks for the question, John. On AETH-401, the subcutaneous Q2W auto-injector has been a game-changer, already capturing 15% share in metastatic NSCLC and extending exclusivity to 2033. Combined with our patent thicket of 18 Orange Book listings and favorable settlements on 70% of ANDAs, we've offset about 60% of the projected first-year erosion. We're confident this positions the franchise to retain significant value post-2027, similar to how we've preserved $1.1 billion YTD across the portfolio.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Yes, John, and the combo expansions with ADCs from our Helix acquisition add another layer, targeting $3 billion peak by 2032.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen, JPMorgan:
Hi, thanks. On the pricing side, with IRA risks looming for AETH-401 post-2028, how are the VBAs performing in real-time, and what's the outlook for net price growth amid biosimilar pressure in Europe?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Good question, Emily. The VBAs on 28% of lives are delivering strong results, with net pricing holding at 68% of WAC thanks to tied rebates on ORR and mPFS from Flatiron RWD. In Europe, despite 22% confidential discounts, we've secured major benefit ratings in Germany and important SMR in France, with NICE in the UK preserving value. We see 7-9% pricing growth into 2025, hedged by pipeline readouts and lifecycle extensions like AETH-401-2.

Operator:
Our next question is from David Patel with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Patel, Goldman Sachs:
Thanks, team. Impressive sales metrics—curious about the rollout of AetherTarget AI internationally and its projected impact on Europe H2 growth, given the slower start there.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
David, thanks. AetherTarget AI has driven 24% better reach in the U.S., and we're expanding it to Europe and Asia by year-end. In Europe, paired with our 450 KOL engagements, we expect 15% sequential acceleration in H2, countering HTA headwinds and boosting NRx share.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
To add, the 4.8x marketing ROI gives us confidence in mid-teens productivity gains full-year.

Operator:
Our final question today comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong, Morgan Stanley:
Good morning. On overall guidance raise, how much is lifecycle management contributing to the offset of the $4.2 billion cliff headwind, and any M&A updates?

Dr. Elena Vasquez, CFO:
Lisa, lifecycle strategies are offsetting 60% of near-term cliff impacts, preserving margins at 38-40%. The $11.2-11.5 billion revenue guide and raised EPS reflect this resilience. On M&A, our $4.2 billion dry powder is active, building on the Helix deal with focus on ADCs and radiopharmas.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Exactly, we're shaping the next wave of oncology innovation.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera, CEO:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Jordan Lee, Vice President of Investor Relations:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Aether Biotech Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
